programme: TRIM28 (KAP1) and EZH2 (catalytic subunit of PRC2) form a facultative-heterochromatin-writing axis: TRIM28 scaffolds SUMOylation-dependent corepressor recruitment while EZH2 deposits H3K27me3, and the two are known to reinforce each other's silencing activity at developmentally-locked loci — TRIM28 recruiting or stabilizing PRC2 occupancy at genes that must stay off once a lineage or stress-response state is set.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease, EZH2/PRC2 activity is reported to suppress oxidative-stress-response genes (GSK126 relief of oxidative stress in AD models) and to be dysregulated in pericyte injury (PHF19-PRC2) and in patient serum, while TRIM28's SUMO-pathway activity has independently been proposed as an AD biomarker signature — together consistent with a corepressor programme that keeps protective, homeostatic and DNA-damage/stress genes silenced in vulnerable neurons and vasculature.
role_in_b: In ocular melanoma, EZH2 shows altered expression in the one retrieved pan-cancer profiling study that includes uveal melanoma, consistent with EZH2's broadly documented role elsewhere in oncology as a driver of a dedifferentiated, invasive state via silencing of differentiation and tumor-suppressor genes; TRIM28 has no retrieved placement in ocular melanoma in this record, so its role here is inferred from its general oncoprotein function rather than shown.
shared_axis: Neurons and uveal melanocytes both derive from neuroectoderm/neural crest and normally use PRC2- and KAP1-based heterochromatin to permanently silence alternate-lineage and stress-response genes during differentiation; under a later pathological stress (oxidative/proteostatic in AD neurons, oncogenic in melanoma), the same corepressor machinery could be re-engaged, silencing protective genes in one tissue and tumor-suppressor/differentiation genes in the other, which would explain concordant TRIM28/EZH2 target-set behaviour without either disease directly causing the other.
reasoning: EZH2 is the only factor in the list independently placed in both diseases by the retrieved record (three AD papers, one pan-cancer paper touching ocular melanoma), and TRIM28's chromatin-corepressor identity gives the pairing a nameable, biologically real module — but TRIM28 itself rests on a single AD paper and no ocular-melanoma evidence, and no retrieved source documents TRIM28 and EZH2 acting together or documents the AD-melanoma link directly, so the connection is inferred from separate disease literatures rather than shown as a pair.
support: 42009747 (TRIM28 SUMO-related biomarker analysis in Alzheimer's disease); 41700920 (GSK126/EZH2 relieves oxidative stress in Alzheimer's disease models); 41825614 (PHF19-PRC2 complex activity in pericyte injury in an Alzheimer's-relevant vascular context); 39073683 (EZH2 and regulatory lncRNAs as a serum biomarker in Alzheimer's disease); 34381492 (pan-cancer expression profiling of EZH2 including ocular melanoma)
how_to_falsify: Perform CUT&RUN/ChIP for H3K27me3 and TRIM28 in patient-derived AD neurons/organoids and in uveal melanoma cell lines, at the shared TRIM28 and EZH2 target sets given here; if the two factors do not co-occupy or functionally cooperate at overlapping loci in either tissue (e.g., EZH2 inhibition with GSK126 fails to alter TRIM28 occupancy or de-repress the same target class in both cell types, or co-IP/PLA shows no TRIM28-EZH2 physical association in either lineage), the shared-corepressor-axis account is falsified.
caveats: Support rests on only 2 of the 12 listed factors — MTA1 (24/32) and ZBTB33 (30/32) are highly concordant but have zero on-topic literature in this record (MTA1's sole paper concerns Parkinson's disease twins, not AD or OM) and are excluded from the programme rather than folded in as unevidenced padding. Brain and uvea are anatomically unrelated but share a neural-crest/neuroectoderm developmental origin, which is the basis for the shared-axis claim rather than direct anatomical adjacency. 32 comparisons draw on only 3 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance counts likely contain non-independent repeats. SOX10 — the master neural-crest/melanocyte transcription factor that would be the obvious anchor for a brain-uvea story — was removed as tissue-generic, along with NOTCH1 and other neural-crest-adjacent regulators; the account deliberately does not lean on it. The single-view list (YBX1, TLE5, SUPT20H, STAT6, TRRAP, LHX3, ZNF274) is not used and none of them overlap with the carrying factors.
